column3: The Hebrew names judgments in the plural; BSB says justice.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says hills in righteousness rather than explicitly bringing righteousness.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew addresses You in the second person; BSB says him.
The Hebrew describes descending and does not separately specify spring showers.
The Hebrew names peace; BSB says prosperity.
The Hebrew says the river without explicitly naming the Euphrates.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew names islands rather than distant shores.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has singular needy and afflicted persons; BSB uses plural descriptions.
The Hebrew names souls of the needy; BSB says lives of the oppressed.
The Hebrew explicitly names their soul and his eyes.
The Hebrew uses an active giving verb with an unnamed giver; BSB uses a passive.
The Hebrew does not separately name fruit trees or forests and says from the city.
The Hebrew describes people blessing themselves in him; BSB uses a passive blessing.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew makes His glory the subject filling the earth; BSB says the earth be filled.
Close to the Hebrew.
